question: A lens of large focal length and large aperture is best suited as an objective of an astronomical telescope since :

options.text: a large aperture contributes to the quality and visibility of the images.
a large area of the objective ensures better light gathering power.
a large aperture provides a better resolution.

solution:
A large aperture collects more light (brighter images of faint objects) and gives better resolving power (resolution $\propto D/\lambda$). Both improve the quality and visibility of the image, and a large focal length gives a high magnification ($f_o/f_e$).

All the statements are true.
